newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen lower on new baht measures.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen lower on new baht measures.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to decline further on Thursday as foreign investors were seen staying on the sidelines after new baht control measures applied this week by the central bank, brokers said.

"The market sentiment is expected to remain poor today as foreigners are not happy with the central bank's moves to prevent foreigners from repatriating baht funds obtained from the bourse," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The SET index declined 5.82 points to a 97-month low of 521.40 on tiny 2.3 billion baht turnover on Wednesday.
Brokers said foreign investors would opt to stay on the sidelines to see if any more new measures were planned by the Bank of Thailand.
Property developer Noble Development Plc NOBL.BK makes its debut on the market on Thursday at an initial public offering price of 16 baht per share.
Brokers said they did not expect Noble Development to perform actively because of the prevailing bearish market.
